label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT: Handover for Thursday's launch

Inês,

My father is ill and I am with my family. I'm taking the train tonight and I don't know for how long, so Thursday is yours. I'm sorry to leave you with this, and sorrier that I found the error in figure 3 only this afternoon, so you are inheriting a mess I should have caught weeks ago. Below is what needs doing and in what order. Everything it refers to is in this folder or in my inbox.

I'll say the other thing now so it doesn't get buried at the end: I trust you completely with this. You know the paper as well as I do. You ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself, and there is nobody I would rather have in my seat on Thursday.

**What went wrong**

Figure 3 and the summary use the 2030 revenue estimate from an old run, one where the free allocation phase-out was not applied. The correct 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does.

- PDF v7 on the drive is already corrected (pages 3, 14 and 15).
- Not yet corrected: the slides (deck v4, slides 6 and 9) and the press release Hanna sent to 34 Brussels contacts on Friday, which says 2.1. It is embargoed until Thursday 10:00, so the release matters most and has to be sorted first.

The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. If anyone asks, please say so plainly. Nobody will think less of you for it, and it is true.

**In this order**

1. **Tuesday morning: the press release, with Hanna.** Ask her to send a correction to the same 34 contacts as soon as possible. It should say clearly that it replaces the earlier release, give 1.4 instead of 2.1, say briefly why (old run, phase-out not applied) and say the conclusion is unchanged. It should go out before Wednesday's press calls, and in any case well before the embargo lifts on Thursday. If Hanna wants a senior name on it, Geert knows I'm away and can sign it off. Ask her to look for 2.1 anywhere else too, such as the website or social posts.

2. **Tuesday: the deck.** Fix the number on slides 6 and 9 and check my speaker notes, which may quote 2.1 as well. Save it as v5 so nobody works from v4. The presentation is now 15 minutes instead of 20, so it needs trimming, and the notes should be in your words, not mine. I'd say the correction out loud in the first minute (see the Kessler section below for why).

3. **Tuesday: make sure v7 of the PDF is the only version anyone can find.** That includes anything printed or handed out on the day.

4. **By Wednesday 12:00: badges.** Tomás Reyes at Lindqvist's office needs the final names of everyone from our side by then, or security won't let them in. Please write to him on Tuesday, tell him you are taking my place as presenter and panellist, and send the names. Include yourself, Hanna if she's coming, and whoever else you want there.

5. **Wednesday 14:00 and 15:00: the two press calls.** They are 20 minutes each by phone, one with a trade newsletter and one with a Belgian daily. Hanna is confirming them. I'd take them as yours, and I'd start both calls by mentioning the correction before they ask. If the corrected release has gone out, they will have seen it. Said first and calmly, it is just a footnote to a good paper. Left for someone else to find, it becomes a story.

6. **Thursday: the event.** Tomás moved the timings because Lindqvist has a vote at lunchtime and leaves at 13:30. The programme now runs:
   - 12:00: guests at the security entrance, badges with Tomás, light lunch outside the room
   - 12:30: Lindqvist welcomes everyone (5 min)
   - 12:35: your presentation, now 15 minutes, so it ends at 12:50
   - 12:50: panel with Dr. Abena Owusu-Mensah (remote), Florian Kessler and you, Lindqvist moderating
   - Lindqvist wants to take at least two questions herself before she leaves at 13:30
   - 13:40 Q&A and 14:00 close were in the original plan. Please ask Tomás who chairs after she leaves, and roughly when he wants the panel to wrap up so her two questions fit in.

   Abena's remote link is in the calendar invite and she tested it with you, so you know it works. It would be kind to send her a short note beforehand saying you are in my seat.

7. **After Thursday: Lucy Tran at the Halvorsen Foundation.** She is attending with a colleague and needs two photos from the event and the attendance numbers for their grant report, ideally by 4 December. Easiest is to ask someone on the day to take the photos and count heads at the door.

**Kessler**

His written comments are in this folder. He has said he will raise two things at the panel, and I think he will try to make the whole event about the first one.

- *The 80% pass-through assumption (section 4).* This is the central case. Annex B runs 40% and 60%, and the result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. You know those runs better than I do, so say this openly and without getting defensive. Concede what is fair: for small manufacturers it may well be lower, and that is exactly why the sensitivity is there. Please don't let him set the tone. After you've answered it once, move on, and if he comes back to it, bring the conversation back to the question of who pays and who receives.
- *Resource shuffling.* We agree it is a risk. It is in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report as the way to track it.

If he tries to use the 2.1 correction against us, you will already have said it first, which takes the force out of it. Abena was strong on our side on the call and will probably back us on the LDC points, so you won't be alone up there.

**One last thing about you**

In Lisbon, when the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel. You did it so calmly that most of the room never noticed anything was wrong. You are better live than you think you are. If something goes sideways on Thursday, whether it's the link, the timing or a hard question, you will deal with it the way you did then.

**Reaching me**

You can call me. Tomorrow after 9:00 I might not pick up, so if I don't, please don't take it personally, and don't wait for me. Decide, and Geert is there if you want a second opinion. Whatever you decide will be fine with me. I'd much rather you make the call than wait for my answer.

Thank you, and again, I'm sorry about the timing.

Marieke
